How your passport works

  1. Mark the places you’ve explored.

    Tap countries on your world map, then go deeper on your UK map, area by area. Search the lists for anything small.

  2. Add the memories you want to keep.

    Note a visit date, what brought you there and what you’d go back for. Memories stay private.

  3. Share your map and choose your next stop.

    Download a world or UK share card for your feed or story, and pin the places you want to see next.

Our Story

The Duo Explorer is about discovering places, noticing the details and collecting stories along the way. This travel passport gives those adventures a place to live.

About The Duo Explorer

Questions

How are countries counted?

Your world map counts 195 countries: the 193 member states of the United Nations, plus Vatican City and Palestine. Other places, such as Greenland, Hong Kong, Puerto Rico, Taiwan and Kosovo, are on the map and can be marked, but they’re shown as other places, not in the 195.

The United Kingdom counts as one country on the world map. Marking any area on your UK map adds it automatically.

How are UK areas counted?

The UK map is made of 361 local authority areas: every council area in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, from ONS data dated December 2024. Each area counts once, and counties, cities and regions aren’t mixed in.

What does the percentage mean?

It’s the share of mapped countries or areas you’ve marked. It isn’t a measure of land covered or of everywhere you’ve been.

Who decides what counts as a visit?

You do. Visits are self-reported. A long trip, a day out or a short stop all count if you say so.

Where is my passport saved?

Both maps, your next stops, memories, photo and settings are saved on this browser, on this device. Nothing is uploaded and there’s no account. Clearing your browser data, or using a private window, will remove it, so export a backup if it matters to you.

How do I move my passport to another device?

Choose “Export backup” to save a file. On the other device, open this page and choose “Import backup”, then select the file. Importing replaces the passport saved on that browser.

How do I download and share a map?

Each map has its own “Share my map” panel. Pick a card design and a size, then choose “Download PNG”. “Share image” opens your device’s share options where they’re supported, and saves the image instead where they aren’t. “Copy caption” copies a ready-made caption.

About these maps

World map

The world map counts 195 countries: the 193 United Nations member states plus Vatican City and Palestine, the two UN observer states. Another 43 places, including overseas territories, Crown dependencies, Greenland, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Kosovo, Western Sahara and Antarctica, can be marked as other places but aren’t in the 195. Northern Cyprus is shown as part of Cyprus and Somaliland as part of Somalia, following UN membership.

Source
Natural Earth, 1:50m Admin 0 countries, simplified for the web. Continents follow the UN geoscheme, with the Americas split into North and South America.
Licence
Public domain.
Note
Borders shown are de facto lines from the source data and don’t imply any position on disputed territory.

UK map

The UK map divides the United Kingdom into 361 areas: the local authority districts used for official statistics. In Scotland these are council areas, in Wales unitary authorities and in Northern Ireland local government districts. Islands are included in the areas they belong to.

Source
Office for National Statistics, Local Authority Districts (December 2024) Boundaries UK, obtained via the Open Innovations geography-bits mirror and simplified for the web.

Not included
